factual_claims.claim: LHV Group reported a record net profit of EUR 150.3 million for 2024, up 7% from EUR 140.9 million in 2023.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group's pre-tax profit for 2024 amounted to EUR 175.1 million and net profit totalled EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: Pre-tax profit increased to EUR 175.1 million, while net income rose 11% to EUR 338.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group's pre-tax profit for 2024 amounted to EUR 175.1 million and net profit totalled EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY). Net interest income grew 8% and net fee income increased 24%. The Group's net income was EUR 338.3 million (+11% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: Net interest income grew 8% to EUR 273.3 million and net fee and commission income increased 24% to EUR 60.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net interest income grew 8% and net fee income increased 24%.

factual_claims.claim: These gains were partly offset by a 14% increase in operating expenses to EUR 146.9 million, mainly because of higher employee numbers and related costs, and by expected credit losses rising to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses amounted to EUR 146.9 million (+14% YoY). Most of the increase in expenses has been related to the increased numbers of employees. Impairments amounted to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million).

factual_claims.claim: The cost-to-income ratio increased slightly to 43.4% from 42.3%, while return on equity declined to 24.5% from 29.0% and net interest margin fell to 3.48% from 3.88%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cost to income ratio %|43.4%|42.3%|... Return on equity (ROE) %*|24.5%|29.0%|... Net interest margin (NIM) %|3.48%|3.88%|

factual_claims.claim: Growth in lending and deposits was the main business development.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The increase in the balance sheet volume was driven by growth in deposit base in all customer segments.

factual_claims.claim: Total assets reached EUR 8.7 billion, up 23%, the net loan portfolio increased EUR 990 million, or 28%, to EUR 4.6 billion, and deposits rose 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Total consolidated assets reached EUR 8.7 billion (+23% YoY). The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY). The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: Corporate lending in Estonia grew 21% to EUR 2.3 billion, Estonian retail loans rose 21% to EUR 1.9 billion, and UK SME lending expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Estonian corporate banking loans increased by 21% to EUR 2.3 billion... Estonian retail loans increased by similar 21%, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion... SME lending in UK picked up in 2024, where the portfolio increased 338% to EUR 348 million.

factual_claims.claim: Management attributed the Group’s profit growth primarily to strong asset growth, cost management and sustained credit quality.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit was at the historically highest level of EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY), an increase of EUR 9.4 million. It was mainly positively affected by the combination of strong asset growth, efficient cost management and sustained credit quality.

factual_claims.claim: However, the share of loans in Stage 2 and Stage 3 increased, and the Group raised impairment allowances as Estonia’s recession continued, although non-performing loans remained at a low level.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The forborne and the overdue portfolio have been increasing in consumer finance and also among corporates throughout the year 2024. As precaution measure, the lending principles have been revised to more restrictive in consumer finance, while impairment allowance levels increased across all credit portfolios... Overdue loans remained at historically low levels throughout 2024, though there was a slight increase during the year. By year-end, the market average share of loans overdue by more than 60 days stood at 0.3%.

factual_claims.claim: The operating environment became less supportive during the year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Estonia’s GDP growth rate in 2024 was still slightly negative and the economy is projected to contract by 0.7% annually in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: The European Central Bank reduced rates four times, and six-month Euribor fell from 3.9% in January to 2.6% in December.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: ECB has lowered capital adequacy requirement by 0.4% valid from 1st of January 2025, and SRB will tell their adjustment in February/March 2025, valid from 2026. ECB has lowered capital adequacy requirement by 0.4% valid from 1st of January 2025, and SRB will tell their adjustment in February/March 2025, valid from 2026. ECB has lowered capital adequacy requirement by 0.4% valid from 1st of January 2025, and SRB will tell their adjustment in February/March 2025, valid from 2026. Every 100 bps increase in interest rates will increase LHV net interest income by EUR 12.5 million within the first 12 months. An equivalent interest rate decrease will reduce net interest income by EUR -34.3 million... The 6-month Euribor, tied to many loan agreements, declined from 3.9% in January to 2.6% in December, with most of the decline occurring in the fourth quarter, aligning with expectations of further policy easing.

factual_claims.claim: LHV stated that falling rates and the repricing cost of deposits negatively affected LHV Pank’s results, while intense competition in both lending and deposits further pressured margins.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Same time interest rates have peaked and started quick lowering. This affects LHV Pank results clearly negatively... During the full year LHV faced with healthy competition for deposits among banks, including heavy competition with targeted offers, as all banks needed to either protect their market share or fund their increasing loan portfolios.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Pank’s net profit declined 1% to EUR 140.5 million despite 6% income growth, reflecting higher expenses, increased credit losses and a EUR 24.4 million deferred tax expense related to expected future dividends.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: LHV Pank’s net profit for the year remained almost the same by decreasing just 1% to EUR 140.5 million. Total income increased by 6%, total operating expenses increased by 12%. ... Results for the year also include EUR 24.4 million deferred tax expense for 2024 payable on the expected future dividend payment.

factual_claims.claim: Its fee income increased 34% due to higher customer activity.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The increase in net fee and commission income was 34%. It was mainly impacted by the higher customer activity.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Bank’s net profit rose to EUR 5.8 million from EUR 5.3 million, supported by 338% loan growth and 195% deposit growth, although results fell short of plan because of slower early-year lending and fluctuating financial-intermediary deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The net profit for the year amounted to 5.8 million, with a return on equity of 7.5%. Profitability for the year fell short of plans due to slower loan portfolio growth at the beginning of the year and fluctuations in deposits from financial intermediaries, which led to lower-than-expected interest income. Loans grew by 267 million over the year, reaching 348 million. Deposits grew by 195% over the year, and the loan portfolio expanded by 338%.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Kindlustus increased net profit fourfold to EUR 1.2 million as premiums grew 21% and the insurance cost ratio improved.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million. Year resulted with strong insurance activity result mainly due to decrease of cost ratio. Additionally, investments income gave substantial impact to company’s profit... The annual gross written premiums were EUR 38.0 million (+21% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: Varahaldus’ profit edged down to EUR 1.6 million, while assets under management rose 3%; no success fee was earned because cumulative fund performance remained below the benchmark.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit of LHV Varahaldus was EUR 1.6 million in 2024... Growth of assets under management continued, both in II and III pillar funds, with asset base growing by 1% in II pillar and by 30% in III pillar in 2024... Benchmark index growth for 2024 was 6.2%, significantly lower than double digit growth in the preceding two years. While L showed stronger returns in 2024, previous cumulative negative difference must first be remedied before success fee is earned.

factual_claims.claim: Paytech’s profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit|0.7|0.5|40%

factual_claims.claim: Capital and liquidity remained strong despite balance-sheet expansion.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: All capital ratios remained strong and well above both the internal and regulatory requirements despite decent growth of risk weighted assets.

factual_claims.claim: CET1, Tier 1 and total capital ratios were 16.89%, 17.96% and 20.68%, respectively, all above requirements.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED

factual_claims.claim: The Group issued EUR 300 million of MREL bonds and EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, while redeeming EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: LHV issued EUR 300 million of MREL eligible bonds in May 2024 and concluded a simultaneous voluntary buyback of the 09.09.2025 bond in amount of EUR 137.17 at the same time. The remainder of the outstanding issue of 09.09.2025 MREL eligible bond in the amount of EUR 62.83 million was called back on call date of 09.09.2024... LHV redeemed EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds and issued EUR 20 million of new Tier 2 bonds.

factual_claims.claim: Management expects near-term profit pressure from lower interest rates but plans continued loan growth and greater operating efficiency.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Although we anticipate a short-term decline in profits due to changes in the interest rate environment, we can offset part of the negative impact through business growth and more efficient operations.
